newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bank deposits rise 6.6 percent in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bank deposits rise 6.6 percent in Oct.

text.p: Venezuelan commercial bank deposits rose 260 billion bolivars ($55 million) or 6.6 percent in October to 4.24 trillion bolivars from September's 3.98 trillion bolivar level, Softline consultants reported.

According to the firm's monthly round-up of 38 commercial banks, 31.7 percent of total deposits were in saving deposits, 40.7 percent in current accounts and fixed-term savings accounted for 24.5 percent.

On the asset side of banks' balance sheets, loan portfolios rose 96.67 billion bolivars, or 6.1 percent, to reach 1.68 trillion bolivars. However that figure was easily topped by investments in securities, which reached 2.40 trillion bolivars.
Current loans accounted for 1.65 trillion bolivars of total loans, restructured loans 44.70 billion bolivars and contested loans 18.69 billion bolivars.
Provisions for bad loans stood at 176 billion bolivars at the end of September, Softline said.

Capitalization rates, the ratio of shareholders equity to total assets, stood at 12.91 percent in October. Meanwhile, the intermediation index, which describes total loans as a fraction of total deposits, stood at 36.76 percent, Softline reported.
